title: Did Russell Crowe Really Accidentally Photograph a UFO in 2013?
excerpt: The actor captured a strange glowing object while trying to photograph fruit bats, sparking theories that still haven’t been fully settled.
content:
In March 2013, Russell Crowe got the internet buzzing when he tweeted a link to a YouTube video with images he claimed he captured of a possible UFO. The timed-exposure photos show what looks like a red-and-yellow object shooting across the sky.

You can check it out for yourself right here:

Shortly after uploading the pictures, Crowe clarified that he and a friend had installed a camera to catch fruit bats outside of his office in Woolloomooloo, Australia, and ended up with that series of shots instead. When skeptics suggested that the supposed UFO was just a reflection of light (perhaps from the beacon on a nearby sailboat), Crowe responded by saying, “The camera is on a balcony, not behind glass.” He also insisted it couldn’t be a lens flare because the object moved and the camera was fixed. 

Russell Crowe Set Up a Camera for Fruit Bats and Somehow Got a ‘UFO’ Instead

Though many shared their theories at the time about what Crowe actually photographed, the object in question—or whatever created the illusion of one—still doesn’t appear to have been identified. One possibility is that it was sunlight being reflected off of an airplane passing overhead. Others were quick to point out that if the UFO had existed outside of Crowe’s camera, other people would’ve inevitably reported seeing it given how heavily populated that part of Australia is.
